title: Request: SM-S9280 (China) / S9280ZCS6DZE2 / kernel 6.1.145
body:
## Device Support Request: SM-S9280 (China) / S9280ZCS6DZE2

### Device details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Model** | Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, **SM-S9280** (China / CHC, TGY, BRI) |
| **Firmware** | `S9280ZCS6DZE2` (One UI 8.5, CHC, May 2026 security patch) |
| **Kernel** | `6.1.145-android14-11-3254743-abS9280ZCS6DZE2` |
| **Bootloader** | Locked — rev 6, OEM unlock removed in One UI 8.x, cannot downgrade |

### Why I think this one is worth adding

The existing S24 Ultra payload (`e3q-S928USQS6DZF2`, SM-S928U) shares the same codename (`e3q`) and the same KMI (`6.1.145`) — so hopefully the port isn't too bad. I know the offsets are firmware-specific and can't be reused, but the shared kernel version should still make this much easier than a from-scratch target.

For SM-S9280 users, this is currently the only way to get root at all: OEM unlock was removed in One UI 8, official BL updates re-lock the bootloader (rev 6, no downgrade), and the patched abl workaround bootloops on the China variant. I tried all of these myself, so this isn't theoretical.

### What I can provide

- Firmware files for `S9280ZCS6DZE2` (already downloaded and extracted)
- Testing on the actual device once a payload is ready

Thanks for the project — happy to help however I can.
